chapters.html:
The soft glow of the computer screens illuminated Mydei’s room, casting gentle pink hues across the walls. Cottage pink, his favorite color, enveloped the space, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. Shelves lined with collectibles from various games and books added a personal touch, while fairy lights twinkled above, enhancing the warmth of the room. It stood in stark contrast to Mydei’s usually serious demeanor, reflecting a softer side of him that he rarely let the world see.

Seated in his gaming chair, Mydei focused intently on the screen. The latest installment of an action RPG captivated him, the game’s vibrant graphics and engaging story pulling him deeper into its world. His fingers danced across the keyboard as he navigated treacherous landscapes, battling fierce enemies while keeping an eye on his chat.

On the side of the screen, a stream of messages flowed, filled with excitement and playful banter.

Chat:

•@Tribbies2.0: “Let’s go, Mydei! Show them who’s boss!”

•@TriNinja99: “How do you even manage to dodge those attacks? Teach me your ways!”

•@TrianneSparkle: “Mydei, you got this! I believe in you!”

•@GamerDude23: “This game is easy, just spam the attack button.”

•@NotYourAverageJoe: “You suck, Mydei. I could do better.”

•@SnarkyCatLady: “Yeah, keep talking, Joe. You’re not even in the game!”

Mydei raised an eyebrow at the chat, his expression shifting from concentration to mild amusement. “Thanks for the confidence boost, guys,” he shot back, his tone dripping with sarcasm. “I’ll just ignore those people in the room.”

He returned his focus to the game, the intensity building as he approached a boss battle. The familiar rhythm of gameplay kept him grounded, though he couldn’t help but glance at the clock ticking away in the corner of his screen.

“Alright, here we go,” he muttered, an edge of determination creeping into his voice as he prepared for the confrontation. The chat exploded with reactions, the atmosphere electric.

Chat:

•@Tribbies2.0: “Don’t mess this up, Mydei! We’re all watching!”

•@TriNinja99: “No pressure or anything!:P”

•@GamerDude23: “I’m placing bets on you failing.”

•@SnarkyCatLady: “Shut up, Joe. You’ll owe me money when he wins.”

•@TrianneSparkle: “You got this! Just don’t die!”

Mydei smirked at the barrage of comments. “I’ll be sure to thank you all for your unwavering support—especially you, Joe. I can feel the love from here.” He leaned into the game, his fingers flying over the keyboard as he engaged the boss.

The tension mounted, and he could feel the excitement radiating from the chat, a mix of encouragement and playful taunts. Moments like these reminded him why he loved streaming—sharing experiences, showcasing his skills, and dealing with the occasional troll who thought they could rattle him.

“Let’s see if you can handle this,” he challenged the boss, his voice steady and focused, fully immersed in the game as he readied for the fight.

-

As the final blow landed on the defeated boss, Mydei leaned back in his chair, a sense of satisfaction washing over him. “Well, that’s one way to wrap up a game,” he muttered to himself, a hint of sarcasm lacing his tone. He wasn’t one for grand celebrations, preferring to keep things straightforward.

Just as he began to navigate away from the game, a familiar username lit up in the chat.

•@Garmentmaker01: “Impressive work, Mydei. Though I expected nothing less.”

Mydei’s brows furrowed slightly at Aglaea’s comment. “Aglaea. What brings you here? Shouldn’t you be busy?” His voice was steady, tinged with curiosity about her unexpected presence.

•@Garmentmaker01: “I needed a moment away from my tasks. Your gameplay is a nice distraction.”

“Glad to hear it’s worth your time,” he replied, his tone dry and measured.

•@Garmentmaker01: “Perhaps you could consider putting a bit more effort into your elegance. A more graceful approach might benefit you.”

Mydei scoffed lightly. “Not likely. I’m more about brute force than finesse.” He could almost feel her disapproval through the screen, playful yet pointed.

•@Garmentmaker01: “That’s unfortunate. But it is, as you say, your style.”

With that, Mydei decided it was time to wrap up the stream. “Thanks for stopping by, Aglaea,” he said, his tone softening just a fraction. “I appreciate it, even if it feels like a waste of your time.”

•@Garmentmaker01: “Always a pleasure, Mydei. Good luck with your next endeavor.”

He nodded, shifting his focus back to the screen, his fingers hovering over the button to end the stream. Just as he was about to click it, a notification pinged from his phone, drawing his attention.

Mydei glanced down, and his expression softened at the sight of the background picture—a candid shot of Phainon. In the photo, Phainon was mid-laugh, his eyes sparkling with joy, sunlight catching the highlights in his hair. He wore a casual outfit that accentuated his lean frame, radiating warmth and happiness. Mydei felt a small smile tugging at the corners of his mouth, admiring how carefree and vibrant Phainon looked.

But that fleeting moment of happiness abruptly halted as reality snapped back into focus. He quickly swiped to end the broadcast, his face returning to its usual serious expression, though a faint hint of warmth lingered in his gaze.

“Alright, that’s it for tonight,” he said, finality in his voice as he clicked the button.

Chat:

•@Tribbies2.0: “Aww, already?”

• @TriNinja99: “GG, Mydei. Night!”

• @TrianneSparkle: “Goodnight, Mydei! Rest well!”

• @GamerDude23: “Mid ending, but whatever, night.”

• @NotYourAverageJoe: “Finally. Took you long enough.”

• @SnarkyCatLady: “Don’t listen to Joe, he’s just mad he lost his bet.”

Mydei let out a quiet sigh, shutting his screen off. The familiar pang of missing Phainon settled in his chest, but for now, he’d have to settle for memories—and the anticipation of his return.

As Mydei leaned back in his chair, finally done with the stream, the quiet hum of his room settled around him. The screen dimmed, the chat no longer filling the space with scrolling messages. He exhaled slowly, stretching his fingers after hours of gaming.

Then—the sound of keys at the door.

A familiar click, the turn of a handle, and then the soft creak as it swung open. Mydei barely needed to glance up to know who it was.

Phainon.

“Finally home,” came the warm, slightly worn-out voice, carrying just a hint of teasing. Mydei heard the door shut behind him, the rustling of fabric as Phainon shifted, kicking off his shoes.

A stretch followed—a full-bodied, indulgent one, punctuated by a sigh of relief. “Long day,” Phainon said, rolling his shoulders. “Exhausting.”

Mydei’s gaze flicked up just in time to see Phainon shrug off the extra layer he’d been wearing—some oversized zip-up hoodie, lazily thrown onto the bed without a second thought. Beneath it, he was dressed to kill.

A fitted, sleeveless top of dark mesh clung to him, sheer in places, teasing glimpses of his toned stomach and the defined lines of his chest. The deep V-cut dipped just low enough to be distracting, and the fabric shimmered faintly under the dim light of the room, catching on every shift of muscle as he moved.

Then—the collar.

A sleek band of black leather sat snug around his throat, a small silver ring resting at the hollow of his collarbone. It gleamed under the soft glow of the room, an accessory that felt more like a statement than an afterthought.

Paired with all of that, he wore tight, tailored pants that sat low on his hips, emphasizing the lean curve of his waist. The smooth, dark fabric hugged his legs just right, every step measured, every motion intentional. Even disheveled from the day, he carried himself like he belonged in the center of attention.

Mydei’s fingers twitched where they rested against his armrest. His gaze lingered—just for a second. Then, with a practiced neutrality, he leaned back.

“Rough day?” His voice was steady, but there was an edge to it, something unreadable.

Phainon just grinned, rolling his shoulders again, muscles flexing under the mesh. “You have no idea.”

Phainon sighed as he rolled his shoulders again, stepping further into the room. “Today was well—” he exhaled, shaking his head with a small laugh as he repeated, “—long.”

Mydei didn’t say anything at first, just watching as Phainon stretched again, his body still shaking off the weight of the day. Without a word, he pushed himself up from his chair, stepping past him toward the kitchen. Phainon didn’t question it, just kept talking.

“First shoot ran over because someone kept fumbling their lines. And I get it, it happens, but then the second shoot got delayed ‘cause of that, and then suddenly everyone’s in a rush to make up for lost time.” He ran a hand through his hair, exhaling. “Then there was this whole thing with the lighting—someone forgot to adjust for the scene change, so we had to reshoot a couple of takes. By then, I was already so damn tired, and—ah, thanks.”

He took the glass of water Mydei held out for him without hesitation, bringing it to his lips. Mydei just settled back onto the bed, watching as Phainon drained half the glass in a single breath.

“Good?” Mydei asked, his voice low, steady.

Phainon hummed in response, setting the cup down on the nightstand before joining Mydei on the bed. Without a word, Mydei shifted slightly, making space for him. It was a quiet sort of care, nothing particularly grand, but it was enough.

“Mm,” Phainon exhaled as he finally let himself relax, melting into the comfort of the bed. Mydei barely hesitated before lifting a hand, fingers threading through Phainon’s hair. Slow, absentminded, the way someone might run their fingers through water.

Phainon’s eyes fluttered shut for a second, a content sigh leaving him. “Careful,” he murmured, teasing, “I might start thinking you like me or something.”

Mydei hummed. “Tragic.”

Phainon huffed a small laugh, the corners of his lips twitching upward. “You’re terrible at denying things.”

Mydei didn’t respond, just kept running his fingers through Phainon’s hair, slow and deliberate. He could feel the way Phainon’s body was finally unwinding, his breathing deepening bit by bit. Whatever teasing remark he might have had, it didn’t make it past his lips. Instead, he let his eyes linger on the curve of Phainon’s smile.

And that was enough.

They stayed like that for a while, neither of them saying much, just resting in the tranquil silence of the room. Mydei’s fingers continued their slow path through Phainon’s hair, and Phainon let him, his body heavy with exhaustion but utterly relaxed against Mydei’s side. The tension from his long day had almost fully melted away, replaced by the warmth of Mydei’s presence.

Eventually, Mydei’s gaze flicked toward his desk. He exhaled through his nose. “Forgot my phone.”

Phainon made a low noise of acknowledgment but didn’t stop him as Mydei shifted, slipping out of bed. He crossed the room with silent steps, reaching for the device still resting on his desk.

Just as his fingers curled around it, he felt the warmth of another presence behind him. Phainon had moved too, slow and easy, pressing in close and resting his head in the space between Mydei’s neck and shoulder, his breath warm against Mydei’s skin.

“Mm,” Phainon hummed, his voice quieter and lower. “What’s the plan for tonight?”

Mydei glanced down at his phone, considering for a moment before responding. “I was thinking dinner,” he said, his tone even and calm. Then, with a slight tilt of his head, he added, “But I can be convinced to do other things.”

Phainon chuckled softly against him, a tired sound that sent a ripple of warmth through Mydei. “That so?”

Mydei didn’t answer right away, allowing the moment to stretch. He let his free hand rest lightly against the edge of the desk, feeling Phainon’s weight against him and the steady rise and fall of his breath.

“Mm,” he finally murmured, letting the quiet settle in again. “We’ll see.”

The atmosphere in the room shifted subtly, a charged energy hanging between them. Mydei shifted slightly, his back pressing against Phainon’s warm body, and he felt Phainon’s breath hitch ever so slightly.

“Dinner can wait,” Phainon murmured, his voice low and teasing. “I’d rather focus on you right now.”

Mydei glanced over his shoulder, a smirk playing at the corners of his mouth. “Oh really? What do you have in mind?”

Phainon’s lips curled into a sly grin as he leaned closer, his breath ghosting over Mydei’s skin. “I’m not sure, but I have a few ideas.” He let his fingers trail down Mydei’s arm, the touch featherlight yet sending a jolt of electricity through him.

“Is that so?” Mydei replied, striving for nonchalance, even as a flush crept up his neck. He turned to fully face Phainon, their eyes locking. “And what makes you think I’d be interested?”

Phainon chuckled softly, a confident glint in his eyes. “You know you’re always interested.” He leaned in, his face inches from Mydei’s, the playful challenge evident in his tone. “You just can’t get enough of me.”

Mydei’s heart raced as he took in Phainon’s relaxed posture, the way his lips curved into a promise of entertainment. “Careful,” he warned, feigning seriousness. “I might think you’ve gotten depraved.”

Phainon arched an eyebrow, leaning in even closer, their foreheads almost touching. “Oh, I think you’re just trying to hide how much you want me.”

Mydei swallowed, the heat rising between them undeniable now. “Yeah? You really want me too, don’t you?” he countered, a teasing lilt in his voice, even as the air crackled with tension.

“Always,” Phainon replied, his gaze unwavering and surprisingly sincere. The space between them felt electric.

Mydei held his breath, caught in the weight of Phainon’s words. “You’re impossible,” he said, attempting to sound stern, but the soft smile tugging at his lips betrayed him.

Phainon’s grin widened, playful and triumphant. “Only because you let me be.”

They stood there for a moment longer, the world around them fading into the background, lost in each other’s eyes.

They stood there for a moment longer, the world around them fading into the background, lost in each other’s eyes. The air was thick with unspoken words, a heady mixture of desire and affection swirling between them.

“Maybe we should…” Phainon began, leaning in closer, their lips almost touching, the warmth radiating off him intoxicating. Mydei’s breath caught in his throat, heart racing in anticipation.

Just then, the chat erupted into a frenzy, completely breaking the moment.

Chat:

•@Peerless Cucumber: “Um…Did I just walk into something?”

@NerdyNightOwl: “OMG, what’s happening?!”

•@Dreamer69: “No way they’re about to kiss, right?!”

Mydei’s eyes widened, realization dawning on him like a bucket of cold water. “Oh fuck,” he muttered, a flush creeping up his neck as he quickly glanced at his screen, confirming his worst fear: the stream was still live.

Phainon, unfazed, merely chuckled and brushed his lips against Mydei’s cheek in a teasing caress. “What’s wrong? Didn’t you want this?” His voice was low, playful, sending shivers down Mydei’s spine.

•@BookishBard: “SOMEONE TELL ME THIS IS REAL?!!”

•@ChaosCuddler: “I’m dying here! They’re so cute (╥﹏╥)”

•@WittyWhisper: “Omg, for free???”

Mydei shot a desperate look at Phainon, who continued to focus on him, seemingly enjoying the moment. “Phainon, they’re watching!” Mydei hissed, his tone a mix of panic and disbelief.

Phainon just smiled, brushing his lips against Mydei’s skin again, his breath warm and inviting. “Let them watch. They’ll just have to deal with it.”

Mydei could feel his resolve crumbling, the heat of the moment pulling him back in. He couldn’t deny the thrill of Phainon’s teasing touch, the way it ignited something deep within him. “You’re impossible,” he managed to say, though his voice was barely above a whisper, caught between frustration and desire.

As the chat continued to spiral into chaos, Mydei found himself torn— caught between the exhilaration of the attention and the intoxicating closeness of Phainon. The room felt suddenly too warm, the situation literally pressing down on him.

“Now, what were we doing?” Phainon murmured, pulling back just enough to meet Mydei’s gaze, his eyes sparkling with mischief.

Mydei swallowed hard, heart pounding. “Maybe we should focus on…”

But Phainon closed the distance again, cutting him off with another playful brush of his lips against Mydei’s, intensifying the spark that had only just begun to flicker.

As the chaotic messages continued to flood the chat, Mydei’s heart raced. The reality of their situation crashed down on him, and he quickly moved to shut down the stream, fingers flying over the keyboard. “Oh fuck,” he muttered under his breath, panic washing over him as it really dawned on him he hadn’t turned it off as he thought originally. The screen finally went dark, the pressure lifting just a bit, but his pulse was still racing.

He leaned back in his chair, trying to calm the rush of adrenaline that had taken hold. It felt like he had just narrowly avoided a disaster.

But the moment of relief didn’t last long. Phainon, ever the contrast to Mydei’s seriousness, burst into laughter, the sound rich and carefree, filling the room with warmth. He didn’t say a word, simply relishing the absurdity of the moment, and his joy was infectious.

Mydei shot him a glare, frustration flickering beneath the surface. “You know we can’t just—”

“Relax,” Phainon said, still chuckling as he settled beside Mydei, the light in his eyes refusing to dim. “That was fun.”

A breath caught in Mydei’s throat, caught between annoyance and the undeniable pull of Phainon’s happiness. The way his eyes sparkled, the ease with which he carried himself—it was hard to maintain his earlier seriousness in the face of such delight.

“Seriously?” Mydei asked, the weight of his earlier tension slowly lifting as he watched Phainon’s grin widen. There was something magnetic about that smile, a reminder of how much he cherished moments like this, even amidst the unexpected.

Phainon leaned closer, his laughter softening into something more intimate. “It’s not every day you get caught in a flirty moment on stream.” He brushed a stray strand of hair from Mydei’s face, a gentle gesture that sent a shiver down his spine.

The simple act broke through Mydei’s irritation. He could feel the corners of his mouth twitching, a reluctant smile threatening to emerge as he met Phainon’s gaze. “You think this is funny?”

“Absolutely,” Phainon said, leaning in closer, their foreheads almost touching. The warmth radiating from him was comforting, disarming. “But I also think it’s an opportunity.”

“What do you mean?” Mydei asked, his voice low and serious yet tinged with curiosity.

“Let’s not let this ruin our fun.” Phainon’s tone shifted, a teasing glimmer in his eyes as he straddled Mydei’s lap, settling comfortably against him. The air between them thickened with unspoken tension, an electric current that seemed to pulse in the silence.

Mydei’s heart raced again, caught off guard by Phainon’s boldness. “Phainon—”

But before he could protest, Phainon closed the distance, capturing Mydei’s lips in a kiss that ignited everything within him. It was soft at first, a gentle exploration that quickly deepened as Phainon’s hands found their way to the back of Mydei’s neck, pulling him closer.

The kiss was a mix of urgency and sweetness, igniting the space around them with a heated intensity. Mydei melted into it, the world outside forgotten as he kissed back with equal fervor, surrendering to the moment.

As they finally pulled away, breaths mingling in the charged atmosphere, Mydei’s earlier seriousness faded completely. The connection between them felt palpable, a bond forged in the laughter and spontaneity of the night.

“Now, that’s what I call fun,” Phainon said with a satisfied grin, his eyes sparkling with excitement.

Mydei felt a surge of warmth in his chest, a smile breaking across his face. As they leaned in for another kiss, he knew without a doubt that he wouldn’t trade this moment for anything in the world.
